## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Mahāpurisalakkhaṇapañha* (“The Question on the Marks of the Great Man”) is a section of the *Milindapañha* (Mil 3.6.3) [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into three modern languages across four translations, including an English translation by John Kelly [SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral identifies a full parallel in the Chinese canon, T 1670b 2.54 (“The Thirty-two Marks of the Buddha”) [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 138 Pali-internal matches across nine different texts, reflecting shared formulaic material concerning the bodily marks of a great man (*mahāpurisa*) [DharmaNexus]. The discourse shares passages with several major canonical suttas treating the marks, including the *Ambaṭṭha Sutta* (DN 3), the *Sela Sutta* (MN 92 and Snp 3.7), the *Lakkhaṇa Sutta* (DN 30), and the *Brahmāyu Sutta* (MN 91) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus aligns passages of the text with later devotional and commentarial literature, showing extensive reuse with the *Buddha-vandanā gantha-saṅgaho Namakkārapāḷi*, the *Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
